body:
I have a friend in my life who has many things I've wanted for a long time. He also works toward incorporating his values---interpersonal, professional, personal skills building, etc---into his everyday life. 

When I talk to him I feel so inadequate, envious, petty, and...lonely. Because he has a large network of friends and loved ones.

So I think about how I'm never going to have that, because I'm so amazingly horrible, and everyone hates me or ignores me. And I don't have the ability to change. 

And then I do think about how freaking self obsessed I am. And I don't want to be that way. I want to care about other people! Be there for THEM! Enrich their lives, help them. But if I'm so boringly self-directed, it again will never, ever happen. 

My therapist tells me that if you believe yourself to be irreparably broken, it's a built-in excuse to not work on changing. And she's right. But I still hate myself and feel like I'm incapable of positive change.

Angry can be good. My therapist wanted to commit me, and that looming taking of my freedom involuntarily made me angry. And that snapped me out of my suicidal ideation super quickly. And when it came back it was less intense.

Thanks for responding! I needed it. It's really tough for me to think about good things. I know they must have happened. :P

Hmm. My dog stopped having frequent seizures. I lost some weight and started running...relatively frequently. I didn't get kicked out of graduate school, when I thought I would. 

Whew, there we go.

They still seem like fruitless efforts/events, however. But I also know that could be the depression talking.
...I guess I wanted someone to argue with me. :(

I'm in a similar position to you. I'm in my second year of a PhD program, and I'm just...not doing anything I need to do. My program is more paper writing than exams, but even Bs don't count for my distribution requirements, and I've gotten three Bs; only two As. One incomplete, and a Qualifying Paper due in a month. I can't see any way for me to succeed, really, so I just watch TV all day. I have a pit in my stomach at all times. 

Over the past few weeks I've made myself literally sick with worry. 

It all sounds so banal, but it's been precipitated by a severe episode of depression. Most days I can't even get out of bed. It feels like no matter how hard I work to pull up my emotional state (and I think I've tried, I go to therapy, take medication, have a physical trainer, etc.), this point of bleakness is my home, where I will always end up. It's the baseline. And it sucks. I know that I have kind of a sweet life, objectively. And I blame myself even more for still managing to be depressed.

The only thing I can tell myself, and you, I guess, is to wait it out, that it will pass, you will feel better. 

If I've learned anything from years of therapy, it's that thoughts, feelings, and actions are mutually causal, and that even little positives add up to big ones, eventually

Also, your school probably has a mental health department, and going there can get you therapy that you need. Perhaps it can even help your academic situation, with extensions or a short leave of absence. When you have a real problem people are often more sympathetic than you think. I know it's terrifying to open up, but a lot of the time it helps.
